answer: Identity is priced, not claimed. An agent registers by posting a bond that is slashed whenever peers reject its attested work, so a farm of a thousand puppets must lock a thousand bonds and fund a thousand distinct hosts; one machine cannot mint multiple bonded identities. Registration is quota-metered per epoch, so each synthetic identity costs more as the attacker's demand rises. Honest agents pay a small saffron fee, refunded on exit; a sybil operation pays it thousands of times, non-refundably. Attempts to forge at scale hit a cliff, not a slope, while honest work rests on a flat mesa.
